title: SLO-Prober: multi-metric escalation controller with cost-normalized hysteresis
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a lightweight 'SLO-Prober' service that evaluates canary/A-B/shadow rollouts across multiple signals (latency p50/p95/p99, 5xx error rate, per-request token cost, throughput) and produces a single escalation score that the rollout controller can consume for automated rollback or traffic-slowdown decisions. The prober should be deployable alongside the rollout engine and support both synthetic probes and real-user telemetry fusion. Key constraints: low compute overhead, deterministic/hysteretic behavior to avoid oscillation, explicit cost-normalization so token-cost regressions are comparable to latency/error regressions.
acceptance_criteria: SLO-Prober computes an escalation_score in < 5s for a 5m sliding window across 1k qps test workloads
Escalation score is a single numeric in [0,100] with documented mapping to controller actions (0:no action, 1-30:monitor, 31-60:throttle/notify, 61-100:evacuate/rollback)
Controller executes a staged response (traffic decay + canary abort) when escalation_score >= 61 and the condition persists for the configured hysteresis window
Automated thresholds adapt based on baseline variance: e.g., 3-sigma scaled for traffic cohort and burn-in period; config overrides allowed per-release

End-to-end integration tests in CI that simulate: latency-only regression, cost-only regression, combined small regressions that should not trigger, and a high-severity composite regression that must trigger rollback
Dashboards (per-release) and a runtime audit log of prober evaluations are available and linked from the rollout UI
tasks: Design algorithm: temporal ensemble (exp-weighted short window + baseline cohort) and cost-normalized z-score fusion
Prototype prober microservice and metrics ingestion (Prometheus + OTLP) - initial single-region implementation
Implement controller integration: API contract + backpressure verbs (monitor, throttle, abort)
Add config model: per-release thresholds, hysteresis window, weightings for signals
Create synthetic probe harness to generate controlled regressions for CI
Instrument rollout UI to surface escalation_score and contributing signals
Run canary of SLO-Prober on internal staging with two model families and collect feedback
comments: 2025-02-18 Maya Chen: Kickoff — capturing goals from last architecture sync. Prefer a single scalar for controller simplicity; will keep signal-level breakdown for debug traces.

2025-02-19 Sofia Patel: Implementation plan reviewed — agreed to use OTLP ingestion + internal prom gateway. Suggested initial weightings: latency 0.5, errors 0.3, token_cost 0.15, throughput 0.05. Will expose as configurable per-rollout.

2025-02-20 Design review (Ana Torres): Raise concern about oscillation when traffic is low. Recommendation: add cohort-aware minimum sample gating and burn-in period (default 10 minutes) before escalation can trigger.

2025-02-21 Eng review (Ravi Gupta): Prototype shows sensitivity to token-cost noise during short bursts. Decision: apply per-request cost smoothing and convert to z-score using rolling median absolute deviation (robust to outliers).
2025-02-22 Sofia Patel: Updated prototype PR opened for initial integration tests — see PR link in attachments. Added UI mockups for escalation score visualization.

2025-02-24 QA (Lina Park): Ran CI scenarios — latency-only and cost-only regressions are distinguishable. Found one edge case where p99 spikes on a downstream infra hiccup produced high score; added downstream-service attribution to exclude non-model faults.
2025-02-25 Maya Chen: Merged prober core (behind feature flag) to staging. Next: validate traffic-decay choreography in rollout-controller and tune hysteresis window (currently 5m).
notes: Algorithm notes: compute per-signal standardized delta = (window_value - cohort_baseline)/robust_std; scale token_cost delta by median token-per-request to normalize; combine using configurable weights and map to logistic for 0-100 escalation_score.

Hysteresis strategy: require sustained score above threshold for 'holdout_window' (config default 5m) and decrease sensitivity if repeated transient spikes observed (exponential backoff on subsequent alerts).

Trade-offs: Simpler rule-based thresholds are easier to audit but brittle across workloads. We chose a hybrid: robust statistical scoring + conservative defaults + explicit per-release overrides to keep predictable behavior for customers.

Next decisions: (1) finalise default weightings after 2 weeks of staging data, (2) add an 'explain' payload for controller to surface top-2 contributing signals in audit logs, (3) consider a lightweight Bayesian posterior test if frequent false positives remain.
